Variance Component Limits for Comparing Several Methods

Source: R/method_vc.R
method_vc.Rd

Fits the variance component model of Carstensen (2010) to measurements of a set of items by two or more methods, with or without replicate measurements, and reports the bias between each pair of methods, the variance components, and limits of agreement (or prediction and tolerance limits) for the difference between single measurements by two methods on a new item.

Usage

method_vc(
  data,
  y,
  method,
  id,
  replicate = NULL,
  replicates = c("exchangeable", "linked"),
  tau = c("common", "method"),
  interval = c("agreement", "tolerance"),
  pred_level = 0.95,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  bound_type = NULL,
  transform = "none",
  include_omega = FALSE,
  keep_model = TRUE,
  control = nlme::lmeControl(returnObject = TRUE)
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format (one row per measurement). Wide data can be converted with mc_long().

y

Name of the column with the measurements.

method

Name of the column identifying the method. The first level (if a factor) or the first value in sorted order is the reference method; differences are reported as earlier minus later level.

id

Name of the column identifying the item (subject).

replicate

Name of the column identifying the replicate. Required when an item is measured more than once by the same method.

replicates

Whether replicates are "exchangeable" (default) or "linked". Replicates are linked when all methods measure an item on the same occasion (replicate r by every method shares the occasion), so measurements on the same occasion share an item-by-replicate effect. This is a property of the design, not of the data.

tau

Whether the method-by-item variance is "common" to all methods (default) or differs by "method". Method-specific values require at least three methods.

interval

Type of limits: "agreement" (default) for limits of agreement with confidence bounds, or "tolerance" for prediction limits and tolerance limits, as in tolerance_limit().

pred_level

The proportion of differences the limits should contain (the agreement level). Default is 0.95.

conf_level

Confidence level for the bias, the variance components, and the confidence bounds of the limits. Default is 0.95.

bound_type

Which claim the confidence bounds of the limits support, "iu" or "joint", as in agreement_limit() and tolerance_limit(). The default (NULL) is "iu" for interval = "agreement" and "joint" for interval = "tolerance". See details.

transform

Transformation applied to the measurements before analysis: "none" (default), "log", "logit", "pctlogit" (logit of a percentage), "sqrt", "asinsqrt", or a list with functions fun and inv (its inverse) and, optionally, a name. All estimates are on the transformed scale.

include_omega

Logical. With linked replicates, whether the item-by-replicate variance (omega) is included in the variance of a difference. Default is FALSE, for methods applied to an item on the same occasion, where it cancels. Use TRUE when the methods would be applied on different occasions in practice.

keep_model

Logical. Whether to keep the fitted model in the returned object. Default is TRUE.

control

Control values for nlme::lme(); see nlme::lmeControl().

Value

An object of class simple_mvc, a list with:

  • bias: tibble with the bias (method1 - method2) for each pair of methods, its standard error, df, and confidence limits.

  • limits: tibble with, for each pair, the bias, the SD of the difference (sd) and its df (df_sd), and the limits (lower_loa, upper_loa, lower_loa_ci, upper_loa_ci for agreement; the standard error of prediction sep, the prediction limits lower.PL, upper.PL, and the tolerance limits lower.TL, upper.TL for tolerance).

  • varcomp: tibble of the variance components (tau, omega, sigma), as SDs and variances, with confidence limits and df.

  • repeatability: tibble with, for each method, the residual SD (sigma), the repeatability coefficient (rc) with confidence limits, and for linked replicates the reproducibility coefficient (rpc) with confidence limits; NULL without replicates. See details.

  • alpha: list with the method means averaged over items (alpha) and their covariance matrix (vcov).

  • vc_cov: approximate covariance matrix of the estimated variances in varcomp.

  • diagnostics: fitted values, Pearson residuals, and predicted random effects, used by check().

  • data: the processed data (columns y, y_t (transformed), method, id, repl).

  • rep_table: the number of items by method and number of replicates.

  • transform: the transformation (functions included).

  • model: the fitted lme or gls model (NULL if keep_model = FALSE).

  • design: list describing the design and settings.

  • call: the matched call, with evaluated settings.

Details

Measurement r of item i by method m is modeled (Carstensen, 2010, eq. 5.1 and 5.2) as $$y_{mir} = \alpha_m + \mu_i + a_{ir} + c_{mi} + e_{mir},$$ with fixed item effects \(\mu_i\), method-by-item effects \(c_{mi} \sim N(0, \tau_m^2)\), residuals \(e_{mir} \sim N(0, \sigma_m^2)\) with a separate SD for each method, and, for linked replicates only, item-by-replicate effects \(a_{ir} \sim N(0, \omega^2)\) common to all methods. The model is fit by REML with nlme::lme().

What can be estimated depends on the design:

  • Replicates: all components. With two methods, only a common \(\tau\) can be estimated.

  • One measurement per item and method, two methods: only the variance of the difference is identifiable. The model is fit with nlme::gls() with a common residual SD, which is the paired-difference analysis of agreement_limit() with data_type = "simple".

  • One measurement per item and method, three or more methods: the method-specific residual SDs (Grubbs-type estimates) absorb the method-by-item variation, and repeatability cannot be estimated. The items are random effects in this case, because with fixed item effects the likelihood is unbounded (one residual SD can shrink to zero).

The bias for methods m and k is \(\alpha_m - \alpha_k\), with containment degrees of freedom (the number of method-by-item cells, minus the number of items and methods, plus one; \((I-1)(M-1)\) with complete data). The variance of the difference between single measurements by the two methods on a new item (on the same occasion) is $$V_{mk} = \tau_m^2 + \tau_k^2 + \sigma_m^2 + \sigma_k^2,$$ plus \(2\omega^2\) with include_omega = TRUE. The limits of agreement are \(\alpha_m - \alpha_k \pm z \sqrt{V_{mk}}\), with \(z = \Phi^{-1}((1 + \code{pred\_level})/2)\). Note that MethComp uses a multiplier of 2.

The uncertainty of the variance components is obtained from the approximate covariance matrix of the variance parameters of the model (the delta method). Confidence intervals for the SDs are Wald intervals on the log scale. \(V_{mk}\) is given Satterthwaite degrees of freedom (df_sd), \(2V^2/\mathrm{var}(\hat V)\), which account for the covariance between the estimated components. With one measurement per item by two methods these are exactly \(n - 1\).

With interval = "tolerance", the prediction limits are \(\alpha_m - \alpha_k \pm t \cdot SEP\), with \(SEP = \sqrt{V_{mk} + SE^2}\) (\(SE\) the standard error of the bias) and \(t\) the \((1 + \code{pred\_level})/2\) quantile of the t distribution with df_sd degrees of freedom, as in tolerance_limit(). They are expected to contain a single new difference with probability pred_level (a beta-expectation tolerance interval), but are not a confidence statement, and they do not depend on bound_type.

The confidence bounds of the limits follow agreement_limit() (interval = "agreement", MOVER bounds) or tolerance_limit() (interval = "tolerance", the tolerance limits), with the same meaning of bound_type:

  • "iu": a one-sided conf_level bound on each limit, for an intersection-union test against a maximal allowable difference.

  • "joint": joint confidence for both limits (agreement), or a pred_level-content, conf_level-confidence tolerance interval (tolerance).

In simulations with 15 to 60 items, 2 or 3 replicates, 2 or 3 methods, and linked or exchangeable replicates (1000 data sets each; 95% targets), the bias CIs had coverage of 0.94 to 0.96. The one-sided bounds of the limits of agreement had 0.92 to 0.96, the joint bounds 0.91 to 0.95, and the joint tolerance limits 0.92 to 0.96; the lowest values (about 0.91 to 0.93) were with 15 items, where the bounds are slightly liberal. The RC intervals had 0.94 to 0.98, and the RpC intervals 0.93 to 0.95.

With replicates, the repeatability coefficient of method m, \(RC_m = z \sqrt{2} \sigma_m\) (Carstensen, 2010, ch. 9), is the limit that the absolute difference between two measurements by the method on the same item, under the same conditions, should not exceed with probability pred_level. Its confidence limits are those of \(\sigma_m\), scaled. For linked replicates, the reproducibility coefficient \(RpC_m = z \sqrt{2} \sqrt{\sigma_m^2 + \omega^2}\) is the same limit for two measurements on different occasions.

References

Carstensen, B. (2010). Comparing Clinical Measurement Methods: A Practical Guide. Wiley.

Carstensen, B., Simpson, J., & Gurrin, L. C. (2008). Statistical models for assessing agreement in method comparison studies with replicate measurements. The International Journal of Biostatistics, 4(1).

Zou, G. Y. (2013). Confidence interval estimation for the Bland–Altman limits of agreement with multiple observations per individual. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 22(6), 630-642.

See also

simple_mvc-methods, method_convert(), sim_methods(), mc_long(), agreement_limit(), tolerance_limit()

Examples

# three methods, linked replicates
dat = sim_methods(n_items = 30, n_reps = 3, methods = c("A", "B", "C"),
                  alpha = c(0, 0.5, -0.2), tau = 0.3, omega = 0.4,
                  sigma = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.4), replicates = "linked",
                  seed = 1)
fit = method_vc(dat, y = "y", method = "method", id = "id",
                replicate = "repl", replicates = "linked")
fit
#> Variance Component Limits of Agreement (LoA)
#> 95% LoA @ 95% Confidence
#> Linked replicates; common method-by-item variance (tau) (30 items, 3 methods)
#> 
#>  Methods Bias    Bias CI            Lower LoA Upper LoA LoA CI

#>  A - C    0.3192 [ 0.1116,  0.5268] -1.0550   1.6934    [-1.3089, 1.9474]
#>  B - C    0.7672 [ 0.5473,  0.9871] -0.7629   2.2973    [-1.0262, 2.5606]
#>  SD    
#>  0.7542
#>  0.7011
#>  0.7807
#>

#>   not a joint 95% interval for the LoA
#> 
#> Variance Components (SD)
#>  Component SD     95% CI          
#>  tau       0.3452 [0.2651, 0.4496]
#>  omega     0.3473 [0.2689, 0.4487]
#>  sigma (A) 0.3261 [0.2483, 0.4282]
#>  sigma (B) 0.4735 [0.3845, 0.5830]
#>  sigma (C) 0.3833 [0.3031, 0.4847]
#>

#>  Method RC     RC CI            RpC    RpC CI          
#>  A      0.9038 [0.6883, 1.1868] 1.3205 [1.1046, 1.5787]

#> RC: limit for the difference between two measurements by a method under the same conditions
#> RpC: the same limit across replicate occasions (includes the item-by-replicate variation)

# two methods, one measurement per item (the paired-difference analysis)
dat2 = sim_methods(n_items = 40, methods = c("A", "B"), alpha = c(0, 0.3),
                   sigma = 0.5, seed = 2)
method_vc(dat2, y = "y", method = "method", id = "id")
